title: A published value written with a decimal comma ('3,75') is read as 375 and its bar is drawn at 375 beside 2.80.
expected: D-15 and AGENTS.md: exact amounts; a value that is not a valid number is a gap, never a different number.
actual: amount() matches /^-?\d[\d,]*(\.\d+)?$/, so any comma placement is a thousands separator. With the first Leverage cell '3,75' the y axis runs to 400 and the bar is drawn at 375 while the other bars sit near zero; the label still reads '3,75'. The same parser feeds every period, stack and waterfall chart on the Forecast tab. Parked under R3 (malformed input).
suggested_change: Require thousands groups of exactly three digits (^-?\d{1,3}(,\d{3})+(\.\d+)?$|^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$) and treat anything else as not plottable.
verify_note: Probe exited 1 with DEFECT PRESENT and the cited code agrees with the cause.
cause: web/src/pages/connected/visuals/visualData.ts:60 - regex accepts any comma placement as a thousands separator.
ruling_note: a wrong figure (3,75 drawn as 375) is High and always repaired (R3); a decimal comma in model-written text is an ordinary input

(no full stop, lower case); the same 'Failed to fetch' appears when the draft cannot be created or the options cannot load.

cause: web/src/pages/connected/start/ReviewSheet.tsx: limits rendered after the echoed inputs.

title: The page leaves a server-side draft behind whenever the form is abandoned, and after 50 drafts every new form fails with 'too many unfinished submissions; try again later' for up to 24 hours.

actual: Three forms abandoned after Continue added 3 drafts (6 to 9). With 50 open drafts the next Continue draws the alert 'too many unfinished submissions; try again later' (lower case), the form cannot proceed, and no control clears the drafts; the service sweeps them only after STALE_SECONDS = 24 hours.

cause: src/deploy_workflow/run_start/submissions.py:178 refusal; :50 STALE_SECONDS=24h; page creates a draft per Continue and never reuses or deletes.

expected: D-32 and D-42: long text wraps in full and never pushes the page wider than the window; a qualification is not truncated.

screen: ColumnsChart with three or more series (maturities by year, recovery by class and case); #/model/*/analysis and the connected Forecast and visuals pages that draw it; checked in a component bundle at 760 px
title: In a group of three or more series, the value label of the middle series is cut off at the top of the drawing when its bar reaches the top tick.
expected: D-15 and D-32: every figure on a chart is shown in full and exact; nothing is cut. The label of a figure is its only direct reading on the chart (the table form has it too).
actual: BarMark raises the middle series' label by MIDDLE_RAISE (16 px) to keep neighbours apart, and BarCanvas leaves 24 px above the plot, so a bar within about 5 px of the top tick puts the label's top 8 px above the svg, and the svg clips it (the '100' above the Notes bar is cut in half). Three series with values 60/100/20 and ticks 0, 50, 100 reproduce it. The connected value ticks bracket the data with round steps, so a maximum such as 100 (a recovery of 100%) lands on the top tick. Whether a real run has such a middle-series value was not checked.
suggested_change: Add MIDDLE_RAISE to the plot's top margin when the group is narrow (or clamp the label's y to the first line inside the drawing).
verify_note: Reproduced with synthetic 60/100/20 data; real-run occurrence unchecked, as the finding says.
cause: web/src/components/chart/ColumnsChart.tsx:44,135 raise of 16 px against the 24 px top margin at BarCanvas.tsx:53.

screen: #/model/transdigm/2025-06-30/front, analysis, statements, forecast, portfolio-fit and limitations (static fixture, debt stack part set to 0)

actual: StackChart throws for a part whose value is not above zero, and the static model reader enforces the same rule ('expected a number above zero'). With the fixture's last part (Receivables facility, 2.2) set to 0, all six model pages of the run read 'This part of the library could not be read' plus the reader's path string; nothing else on the run is shown. The connected app avoids this with its own hand-built flex bar for stacks that contain a zero (a second drawing of the same chart, in charts.tsx). Whether the exporter ever emits a zero part was not established: its code is not in the repository.
suggested_change: Let StackChart draw a zero part (a legend row and no segment, as the connected fallback does) and relax the reader to 'zero or more'; keep the throw for a negative value. S5 owns the reader line.
verify_note: Reproduced with a fixture edit; whether the exporter emits a zero part is unestablished, so Medium rather than High.
cause: web/src/pages/model/slice/read-sections.ts:249 and web/src/components/chart/StackChart.tsx:58 reject zero.

screen: / (library index), partial data (entry without metrics, index without workspace)
title: One malformed catalogue entry takes down the whole Library page: the user sees only 'This page could not be loaded' and a Reload button that fails the same way.
expected: D-31: a failed region is contained and says what failed; a record that cannot be drawn is not allowed to blank the home page. HeadlineFigures types metrics as required (publishedReport.ts:196-209) but the service is the only guard.
actual: A /connected/library answer whose entry lacks `metrics` throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading net_leverage)' inside HeadlineFigures (HeadlineFigures.tsx:16); an answer without `workspace` throws in MatchRuns (LibraryIndex.tsx:30). ConnectedLoadBoundary replaces the whole page, including the navigation rail, with the heading 'Credit OS', one sentence and Reload page. The entry fields are used unchecked: `[newest.name, newest.issuer, …].some(v => v.toLowerCase()…)` (LibraryIndex.tsx:58-61) also throws on any undefined text field. Browser-intercepted payloads only; the real service always sends these fields.
suggested_change: Validate the index once in getLibraryIndex (reject with the 'could not be loaded' message) or wrap each card in its own error boundary; this is parked as hostile input.

screen: /runs and /run/<id>, partial data (status, module state or event kind outside the vocabulary)
title: A run status, module state or event kind the client does not know crashes the whole Run activity or run page into the load-failure screen.
expected: api.ts:92-97 says the service 'sends these words and no others' and tests/test_react_frontend.py holds them; a newer or older service must still leave the page readable (D-31, no blank or crashed screen).
actual: EndedTable calls StatusBadge with ENDED[run.status] (RunActivity.tsx:191); an unknown status gives `unknown status state "undefined"`, thrown by StatusBadge, and the whole page is replaced by 'This page could not be loaded'. The same happens for a module state outside waiting/running/done/stopped (STEP[state], RunActivity.tsx:117) and for an event kind outside MILESTONES (runFigures.ts:116 destructures undefined: 'undefined is not iterable'). Run activity re-reads every 5 s, so one bad record hides every run. Browser-intercepted payloads only.
suggested_change: Fall back to a neutral 'Unknown state' badge and a generic feed line for words outside the tables; parked as hostile input.

screen: / (library index) and /report/<folder> (report frame), error: non-JSON answer
title: getLibraryIndex and getSnapshot hand the browser's JSON parse error to the reader ('Unexpected token '<', "<html>oops</html>" is not valid JSON').
expected: D-31: no raw error string. api.ts request() already guards this case (api.ts:173-193: json().catch(() => null), then a plain sentence), so the two publishedReport fetchers are inconsistent with it.
actual: publishedReport.ts:248-259 call `response.json()` unguarded; when the service answers 200 with a page that is not JSON (an interposed proxy, a half-written file) the ErrorNotice shows the SyntaxError text. Seen on the Library page with an intercepted answer.
suggested_change: Reuse request() (or the same json().catch) in both fetchers so every failure reads as a sentence.

title: Every connected page except the report is titled 'Credit OS', so tabs, history entries and screen-reader page announcements cannot tell Library, Run activity and a run apart.

title: Spend and cap are rounded through binary floating point, so an exact decimal ending in 5 can show one cent low ('3.105' draws USD 3.10).

Only exact ties are affected, and amounts settle in many decimals, so it is rare; the bar value is clamped to the cap separately (Math.min).
suggested_change: Round the decimal text itself (string arithmetic or a decimal helper) instead of a float.

title: Run form level offers Standard, which behaves exactly like Basic.

title: Document refusals change the case of a file name and quote raw parser text.
expected: Source identities are shown exactly (AGENTS.md: preserve source identities); D-31: plain wording.

(the launcher-line capitaliser changes the name); notes.docx gives 'Cannot read notes.docx: File is not a zip file'; image.png gives 'The uploaded documents: no readable issuer file'. One unreadable file blocks the whole reading, and every row keeps the grey 'Selected' badge.

title: The 50 MB limit in the drop-zone hint is not checked when a file is chosen; a 52 MB file is uploaded in full and refused with a message that names no file.
expected: The drop zone supports maxSize and onSizeLimitExceed (file-upload-base.tsx:30-36,110-126); a stated limit is checked at selection.
actual: big52.txt (52 MB) is listed as 'Selected'; Inspect sends the whole file and the service answers 400 'a file is at most 50 MB', shown at the top of the card with no file name and a console error.
suggested_change: Pass maxSize (50 * 1024 * 1024) and an onSizeLimitExceed handler that names the file.

title: Choosing the same file or folder twice lists it twice, and the problem is reported only at Continue without naming the row.
expected: Duplicate selections are caught when added, or the refused row is marked.
actual: Choosing a folder twice (or two files with the same name) lists both rows; Inspect or Continue then draws 'Choose documents with distinct file names.' while every row still says 'Selected'.
suggested_change: Skip a file already in the list (same name, size and modified time) and mark duplicates by name.
cluster_cause: the same file chosen twice is listed twice and refused only at Continue or Inspect without naming the row

title: The Issuer ID rule is never stated, the derived ID drops letters such as Ø and is empty for non-Latin names, and only the browser's native bubble reports it.
expected: CT-002: pattern [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}; the analyst is told the rule before the browser refuses.
actual: 'Ørsted A/S' becomes 'rsted-a-s'; 'Эрикссон' and '日本電信電話' give an empty required field; 'Northbridge Group' typed into the ID gives only 'Please match the requested format.' The page's own sentence 'Enter an issuer name and an issuer ID using letters a–z, digits or hyphens' is reachable only for a name of spaces (native required/pattern block first).
suggested_change: Add help text under Issuer ID with the rule and transliterate Ø, ß and similar before dropping characters.

title: Your name is required but not marked, and its rule is checked only at Review run, after three steps.
expected: CT-009: required; the rule shown with the field (it is, as help text) and the field marked required before the analyst moves on.
actual: The field has no required or aria-required; 'bad' passes Documents, Purpose and Context and only the Review run press returns the analyst to Documents with the alert (focus lands on the field and the 1-problem button works).
suggested_change: Check the name when leaving Documents and mark the field required.
cluster_cause: Your name is required but not marked; checked only at Review run

title: Stepper notes, field help, pathway module counts, document badges and the drop-zone hint are set at 12 px.
expected: D-30: nothing written here set below 13 px.
actual: Computed font size 12 px on 'Add files', 'Choose one', 'Optional', 'Paid step', '5 base modules' and the other seven chips, 'Selected', 'Three uppercase letters.', 'Your short label…' and the 'Add filings and other source documents' hint (4 to 39 elements per screen).
suggested_change: Raise these to the 13 px caption size.

title: All eight pathway cards carry the same file-check icon, which says nothing about the pathway.
expected: D-20 (no decorative icons that carry no meaning) and D-03 (do not reuse one design for unlike items).
actual: Every card header draws FileCheck02 in the same brand tile; the cards differ only by title, one sentence and the module count.
suggested_change: Drop the icon or use one that names the pathway's purpose.

title: 'I accept these 6 limits' counts every affected module, while the card shows one limit and an 'Also affects' list.
expected: The wording matches what the analyst can see; the page's own counters say '0 of 4 decided'.
actual: One 'Will refuse' card (Legal & covenants) lists five more modules under 'Also affects'; its checkbox reads 'I accept these 6 limits', and the readiness counter counts it as one of 4 decisions.
suggested_change: Word it 'I accept this limit and its 5 consequences'.

title: 'Add facility', 'Add quote', 'Add rating' and the other Add buttons disable at their maximum with no reason.
expected: D-31: a disabled control says why.
actual: Add facility stops after 20 rows; the button is disabled with no sentence about the maximum.
suggested_change: Show 'Most 20 facilities' beside the disabled button.

title: With documents waiting to be carried the list says 'No documents yet.' while Continue and Inspect are enabled.
expected: The list or a sentence names what will be copied.
actual: The earlier run's three documents appear only after Inspect or Continue; before that the card reads 'No documents yet.'
suggested_change: Show the carried file names (from prior.files) as 'Will be copied' rows.

title: An unknown or malformed from= run shows the service's raw words 'unknown run' or 'not found' in a quiet status line.
expected: D-31: no raw error string; say the earlier run could not be found and that this is a new form.
actual: ?from=does-not-exist shows 'unknown run', ?from=../../etc/passwd shows 'not found', both as muted role=status text; the form opens blank.
suggested_change: Replace with 'The earlier run could not be found. Starting a new form.'

title: Choosing a different pathway silently clears the Requested modules selection.
expected: The analyst is told when a choice already made is reset.
actual: Unchecking one of 20 modules under Deep, then choosing Full on Purpose leaves all 14 checked with no message.
suggested_change: Say 'Module choice reset for the new pathway' (role=status).

title: A service sentence reads 'This pathway does not produce the What changed since the last Report report section.' and the same part of the report has two names on the sheet.
expected: Reader-facing wording is plain and one name per thing (D-16).
actual: 'No action needed (1)' shows the sentence above, 'Report sections omitted · What changed since the last Report' is drawn under Purpose and modules, while the module list of a run with an earlier run names the same part 'Changes since the last run'.
suggested_change: Write 'This pathway does not produce the "What changed since the last Report" section.' or use one name.

title: A Submit answered 200 without a run id navigates to /run/undefined.
expected: A reply without a run id is an error shown on the review, not a navigation.
actual: With the submit reply {status:'queued'} the page navigated to /run/undefined (the Run page then said 'unknown run' and called /connected/activity/undefined, 404).
suggested_change: Check typeof id === 'string' and a non-empty id before navigating.

title: One unbroken 336-character token in the lead Bottom line runs past the navy band and makes the main region scroll sideways.
expected: Long text wraps in full; a qualification is never truncated (design-rubric D-32). FindingParagraph already uses wrap-anywhere.
actual: The lead is drawn as an h2 with no wrap-anywhere; the h2 is 1,158 px wide with 3,702 px of content, main.scrollWidth 3,808 against 1,372 client width; the text is cut at the band edge.
suggested_change: Add wrap-anywhere (and min-w-0) to the BottomLine lead and rest.

title: The heading outline does not follow the page structure: the whole Bottom line paragraph is the h2 (no 'Bottom line' heading text), module sections are h2 siblings of the module name h2, and Changes has no h2 of its own in its first-run state.
expected: One h1 per page and headings in order that describe the structure (design-rubric D-36): module name h2, its sections h3; a heading that names the Bottom line.
actual: Overview: H2 'Overview', H2 '<the bottom line sentence>', H2 'Key findings'. Modules/CP-2A: H2 'Downside', H2 '<bottom line sentence>', H3 chart titles under that sentence, H2 'Key findings', H2 'Limitations', H3 'Monitoring sensitivities' under Limitations. Changes (no earlier run): H1, H2 'No earlier run to compare.'.
suggested_change: Render the band label as the heading and the lead as a paragraph; use h3 for sections on module pages.
ruling_note: R16 (owner, 2026-11-17: 'screen reader - not required'): a finding that changes only what a screen reader announces is not a defect; any reviewed fix already merged stays

title: A change card shows a positive difference without a sign ('0.80x') while the Overview tile for the same measure shows '+0.80x vs FY2023'.
expected: Sibling screens agree (design-rubric D-26); signature of the year-on-year difference is this-year-minus-last-year with the sign (D-45; signal.ts changeText adds '+').
actual: Changes.tsx passes `withUnit(measure.difference, unit)` (publishedReport.ts:381) which never adds '+'; negative differences carry '-', positive ones carry nothing.
suggested_change: Use changeText for the card's difference.

title: When CP-8 delivered, the same handoff is drawn twice: on the Changes tab and again as a module 'Changes since the last run' in the Modules navigator, counted in the Modules tab badge.
expected: AGENTS.md: CP-8's handoff is shown in the library's Changes page; content-matrix CM-114 puts it on Changes (and Evidence).
actual: With a CP-8 output in the run the Modules tab reads 'Modules 15', the navigator lists 'Changes since the last run' and its page draws the same Bottom line, Key findings and Limitations ledger as the Changes tab.
suggested_change: none: the owner decides whether CP-8 stays listed as a module; if not, filter it out of buildReportView.modules.
ruling_note: OQ-10 decided (R10): show CP-8 on Changes only, not as a module

title: The Chart/Table and Cards/Table switches are role=radiogroup buttons whose arrow keys move focus without selecting and whose radios are both Tab stops.
expected: ARIA radio pattern: arrow keys move and select, one Tab stop for the group (design-rubric D-35). Component is shared (X1).
actual: Focus on Chart, ArrowRight: focus moves to Table, aria-checked stays false until Space; both radios have tabIndex 0. 32 radiogroups on the 14 module pages plus the Changes presentation switch.
suggested_change: Use a RadioGroup/ToggleButtonGroup with selection following focus, or label the control as toggle buttons (aria-pressed) instead of radios.
ruling_note: R14 (owner, 2026-11-17: 'only pc, no need for keyboard'): the app runs on desktop PCs with a mouse; narrow-screen, touch and keyboard-only findings are not defects; any reviewed fix already merged stays
cluster_cause: ButtonGroup radiogroup: arrow keys move focus without selecting, both radios are tab stops (button-group.tsx)

title: Controls repeat identical accessible names with no context: 'Show sources for this passage' (several per module page) and six links named 'Evidence' on Overview.
expected: Every control has a distinguishable name (design-rubric D-37).
actual: Overview has 'Evidence' x6 (five Dates-to-watch rows and the tab) and 'Show sources for this passage' x2; CP-6 has 5 of the latter. A screen-reader user cannot tell the paragraphs apart.
suggested_change: Name the control after its section, e.g. 'Show sources for Key findings'; name each date link after its event.
ruling_note: R16 (owner, 2026-11-17: 'screen reader - not required'): a finding that changes only what a screen reader announces is not a defect; any reviewed fix already merged stays
cluster_cause: trace controls share generic accessible names (TraceControl naming)

screen: /report/<run>#overview, lead other than the committee decision (full)
title: The disclosure that holds the lead's second Bottom line paragraph is always labelled 'Decision rationale', also when the lead is Fundamental credit or Earnings update.
expected: Labels carry information (design-rubric D-16); CM-037/038 name three possible leads.
actual: With CP-6 not assessable, CP-2 leads and its second paragraph sits behind a closed 'Decision rationale' disclosure; the paragraph is hidden by default on Overview.
suggested_change: Label it by the lead ('Credit view, continued') or show the second paragraph; the wording and the default state are the owner's.
ruling_note: the ruling and CM-037/038 name the lead kicker; follow them

screen: /report/<run>#overview, lead Bottom line that cites a source (partial)
title: When the lead Bottom line holds a source reference, the navy band is lost: the heading 'Bottom line' is followed by the five figure tiles and then a link 'Read this passage in Evidence'.
expected: Bottom line first and as the band (D-01, D-22, CM-001); figures follow it.
actual: drawSection falls to the generic card for a passage with a reference; `afterBottomLine` (the figure tiles) is placed between the card heading and the paragraph, so the tiles read as the bottom line. Cards sit inside a card.
suggested_change: Draw `afterBottomLine` after the paragraph in the fallback card, and keep the band with a 'Read in Evidence' link as its text.

title: The three 'no comparison' sentences (not produced, not compared, no comparison recorded) and the unreadable-comparison sentence carry no link; only the first-run state offers 'Open the Overview'.
expected: CM-051: a fixed sentence states the case; the service's reason is drawn on Evidence. The reader should be able to reach that reason (D-31).
actual: A page holding only a heading and one sentence, no action to the Overview or the Evidence where the reason is drawn.
suggested_change: Add 'Open the Overview' and 'Review comparison evidence' links to those states.

title: On Overview the trace control of each 'Bottom line by module' row sits alone on a third line under the paragraph, unlike every other paragraph where it sits at the right of the text.
expected: Sibling screens agree (design-rubric D-26); 13 identical stacked rows (D-03).
actual: Each of the 13 rows is title+badge, one sentence, then a lone icon button; the page is 4,171 px tall.
suggested_change: Put the PublishedSource control beside the sentence (flex row), as FindingParagraph does.

title: The Modules navigator's <aside> has no accessible name, so the page has two unnamed complementary landmarks (axe landmark-unique); the 'Modules 14' tab has a name that does not contain its visible text 'Modules14'.
expected: Landmarks are distinguishable; accessible name contains the visible label (WCAG 2.5.3; design-rubric D-37).
actual: axe-core 4.x on 5 module pages at 1440 and 390 px: landmark-unique (moderate) and label-content-name-mismatch (serious, 'Modules 14', the frame's tab) on every page.
suggested_change: Give the aside aria-label='Module navigator'; give the count badge a leading space or build the label from the visible text.
ruling_note: R16 (owner, 2026-11-17: 'screen reader - not required'): a finding that changes only what a screen reader announces is not a defect; any reviewed fix already merged stays

title: The change cards are cards inside the 'Changes since the last run' card.
expected: No cards inside cards; not every box is a card (design-rubric D-21).
actual: `section.card` (rounded border, shadow) wraps a grid of ChangeCard `li` boxes, each with its own border and radius; the same happens for the Cards/Table switch row. Overview figure tiles inside the fallback Bottom line card repeat it.
suggested_change: Let the cards stand on the page (heading outside any card) or use plain rows inside the section card.

title: The Modules navigator has no search at its top.
expected: Ruling 2026-11-11 decision 5, content-matrix CM-028 and control-matrix CT-044: 'search sits at the top' of the navigator, beside the On this page outline and, on narrow screens, a labelled picker.
actual: The aside opens with the 'On this page' outline; 0 input, search or searchbox elements; the 14-module run is navigated by the list only. ModuleNav has no search code.
suggested_change: Add the search field to ModuleNav (filters the module list by plain name), or record that the owner dropped it.

title: The lead band on Overview is labelled 'Bottom line'; the ruling and the matrix name its kicker 'Credit view' ('Earnings view' on an Earnings Update).
expected: Content-matrix CM-037 ('lead section kicker Credit view') and CM-038; ruling 2026-11-11 H5 amendment 2026-11-16: the kicker reads 'Earnings view' in place of 'Credit view'.
actual: findingLabel() returns the section heading 'Bottom line' unless overviewLabel is set; only CP-1B sets it ('Earnings view'). 'Credit view' appears nowhere in web/src.
suggested_change: Pass overviewLabel='Credit view' for CP-6, CP-2 and CP-L10 leads (a wording choice the owner may confirm).
ruling_note: the ruling and CM-037/038 name the lead kicker; follow them

title: The document title is 'Modules — <issuer> — Credit OS' for every module, and a module change is neither focused nor announced.
expected: A page title that identifies the content (WCAG 2.4.2) and a status change announced without moving focus (design-rubric D-43).
actual: Titles for Financial foundation, Downside and Committee decision are identical; after choosing a module there is no [aria-live], role=status or role=alert region on the page.
suggested_change: Add the module name to the title and move focus to the module heading (also fixes C3-002).

title: 'Compare with the 5% move' on Rates, FX and hedging is a <select> with one option ('10%'), so the control offers no choice.
expected: A control the reader can operate changes something; a one-choice selector is a fixed label (design-rubric D-03, D-35). The code is in visuals/MacroSensitivity (C4) and shows on this C3 module page.
actual: The select holds the single option '10%'; selecting it changes nothing (checked: content identical). The two Downside selectors ('Compare with', 'Cash-interest basis') have two options each and change the panel.
suggested_change: Draw the selector only when it has two or more options; otherwise print 'Compared with the 5% move: 10%'.
cluster_cause: 'Compare with the 5% move' is a select with one option (MacroSensitivity.tsx)

title: Text is set at 12 px on report pages: the Source readiness 'key limitation' reasons, the navigator's group captions, chart labels (70 SVG text nodes on Financial foundation) and the Committee decision limit labels.
expected: Nothing set below 13 px (design-rubric D-30); a qualification is never smaller or fainter than the text it qualifies (D-32).
actual: `text-xs text-text-tertiary` on the reason under each readiness group ('Only the synthetic filing is available', 'Financing terms are absent') is 12 px; 'On this page' and 'Modules in this run' captions are 12 px; every chart axis and value label is 12 px. The tab count badge is 12 px (a source component, exempt).
suggested_change: Raise those classes to the 13 px caption size; chart text is C4's.

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (full), base case basis note (state: model unit USD millions, zero-input limitation)
title: The 'base case basis' sentence prints two figures without a unit and the third as '$62.00m', and its trigger text is emitted by nothing in the repository.
expected: D-15 and CM-022: every figure carries its currency or unit; one unit form across the page (CM-320).
actual: Rewritten in the browser from a model limitation and a Calculations ledger, the card reads 'The calculation gives 132.00 cash proxy. The handoff gives 194.00 free cash flow. The displayed difference is $62.00m.' The first two figures are unitless, the third uses '$...m' while the rest of the page says 'USD millions', and the sentence says 'handoff'. The branch needs a model limitation matching /machine input is set to zero/ and ledger rows 'Base FCF <FY>' and 'Base taxes and working-capital inflow <FY>': a search of src/, tests/ and docs/ finds the phrase only in web/src test fixtures, so no producer in this repository reaches it (branch that no current input reaches; if a live handoff does, the defects above apply). The canned run does not reach it; it was exercised with an intercepted snapshot (labelled state, not a live case).
suggested_change: Either remove BasisNote and the zero-input regexes if no handoff produces them, or draw all three amounts with withUnit(...) and drop 'handoff'.

title: The Chart/Table toggle is a radiogroup whose arrow keys move focus without selecting.
expected: D-35 and the ARIA radio pattern: arrow keys move focus and select in a radiogroup.
actual: With 'Chart' focused, ArrowRight moves focus to 'Table' while Chart stays aria-checked=true and the figure does not change; Space or Enter is then needed. Same on all 15 Forecast toggles and the Calendar toggle. The component is the shared ChartFrame (X1 owns the file).
suggested_change: Select on arrow (React Aria ToggleButtonGroup with a radio-style selection) or use role=group with aria-pressed buttons.

title: Trace controls share accessible names: three 'Show sources for Cash proxy by scenario', and 'Show sources for FY2023' (and FY2024, FY2026, FY2027) repeated across figures.
expected: D-37 and CM-009: one labelled trace control per row, each with its own accessible name.
actual: The chart header control and the two Scenario comparison rows (Base case, Downside shock) all read 'Show sources for Cash proxy by scenario' (the table passes the same `source` node to every row). Row controls in the Table form of the run charts are named by the row label alone, so 'Show sources for FY2023', 'FY2024', 'FY2026' and 'FY2027' each repeat across 2 to 4 figures (27 table-row controls checked; all open and return focus). The drawer also holds two buttons named 'Close' (the icon and the footer button).
suggested_change: Name each row's control by its case ('Show sources for Base case cash proxy').

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (partial: a case's last cash proxy is not a value)
title: A case card whose cash proxy is missing reads 'Not available' with no reason, while the table beside it gives the reason and uses 'n.a.'.
expected: D-14 and CM-023/CM-066: a missing figure is 'n.a.' with its reason, never silent.
actual: With the Downside cash proxy cell set to na ('Not calculable: cash is negative before funding'), the card shows 'Not available'; only the Scenario comparison cell shows the reason.
suggested_change: Show 'n.a.' and the cell's reason on the card.

title: The yield value in the Securities comparison chart wraps its unit onto a second line and keeps four decimals.
expected: CM-022 (at most two decimals in prose) and D-32 (nothing broken): '7.0100%' should read on one line; the handoff gives '7.01% rounded'.
actual: The label is drawn '7.0100' with '%' on the next line (box 56 by 44 px, line height 22 px) beside a chart bar; the card above reads 'yield 7.0100%, 7.01% rounded'.
suggested_change: Draw the rounded text and widen the value column, or keep the unit with the number (no-wrap).

title: A lone 'x' is drawn under the Leverage and Interest cover charts as their unit note.
expected: D-16/D-26: unit notes read as words ('US$m', 'times').
actual: The figure caption is the one letter 'x' (Leverage, Interest cover) while money charts read 'US$m'; it looks like a stray character.
suggested_change: Label the unit 'x (times)' or show it in the axis title.

title: The same money unit is written four ways across the C4 screens: 'USD millions', 'US$m', '$m' and '$62.00m'.
expected: D-26 and CM-320: one unit form per report.
actual: Forecast model: 'USD millions' (or 'Units not recorded'); run charts: 'US$m' (as published); Downside, rate/FX and break-point comparisons: 'Stressed FCF ($m)', 'Change in debt ($m)' (unitLabel); basis note: '$62.00m' (withUnit).
suggested_change: Choose one rendering (the issuer's code plus 'm') and apply it through unitLabel/withUnit everywhere.
cluster_cause: the connected report writes the same money unit several ways (publishedReport.ts)

title: The calendar's year markers are 14 by 14 px, are not tab stops and cannot be pressed at 480 px or less.
expected: D-41: pointer targets at least 24 by 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8) unless an equivalent control exists.
actual: 36 marker buttons measure 14 by 14 px, tabindex -1, pointer-events none at 390 px. The details row buttons (28 px) give the same information, so this is a polish defect.
suggested_change: Size the marker hit area to 24 px or drop the marker button role at narrow widths.
ruling_note: R14 (owner, 2026-11-17: 'only pc, no need for keyboard'): the app runs on desktop PCs with a mouse; narrow-screen, touch and keyboard-only findings are not defects; any reviewed fix already merged stays
cluster_cause: calendar and timeline markers are 14 by 14 px, under the target size

title: At 390 px the Scenario comparison table and the model grid are clipped without a scroll cue, and the Scenario comparison region is not keyboard-reachable like the model grid.
expected: D-42 and D-35: content reflows without loss; a scrollable region is focusable and named.
actual: Scenario comparison has scrollWidth 420 in a 316 px box (the FY2027E column is cut off) with tabIndex -1 and no role or label; the Cash flow model container is role=region, labelled and tabIndex 0. Published exposures (inside the closed details) uses the same ChartTable wrapper. The model grid at 390 px also shows two of three forecast years (its sticky 'Line item' column takes about 45% of the width) and cuts FY2027E in half with no fade or hint that the region scrolls; its container is focusable and named, so the keyboard path exists.
suggested_change: Give the ChartTable wrapper role=region, an aria-label and tabIndex 0 when it overflows.

title: Chart axis labels (131 SVG text nodes on the Forecast tab), the limits chart labels and the 'On this page' label are 12 px.
expected: D-30: no text under 13 px.
actual: Computed font size is 12 px for every chart axis label, 'limit 2.50%', '2.37%', 'Max single issuer exposure' and 'On this page'.
suggested_change: Raise the chart label size to 13 px; use text-small for the nav label.

title: The Forecast tab shows no case drivers on the case cards and no deleveraging or break-point timing; drivers appear only as grid rows and the assumptions sit in a closed details.
expected: CM-065 (forecast cases with their drivers), CM-165 (driver comparison), CM-164 (deleveraging and break-point timing on Forecast).
actual: Cards show cash proxy, period, unit and the note only. 'Forecast assumptions' is closed by default and, for the canned run, holds only 'Observed / Not supplied: nothing to report'. T2H.7 and T2H.8 are not drawn on the Forecast tab at all (only model.register, T2H.3, is). The synthetic run holds no driver data, so the exact gap for a live run is not verified.
suggested_change: Name the driver basis on each card and draw the break-point timing, or amend the matrix.
ruling_note: CM-065/164/165; draw what the handoff holds, state a gap where it holds nothing

title: Period series (leverage, interest cover, liquidity) are drawn as grouped columns; a line is used only when a value is negative.
expected: D-02 and CM-122/123/124: a trend as one line (C2) or multi-series paths (C3).
actual: periods() returns TrendChart only when `values.some(v < 0)` (charts.tsx:97); otherwise ColumnsChart. Two periods read acceptably as columns; with several periods a line would show the path the matrix asks for.
suggested_change: Choose the form from the descriptor's kind (trend) rather than from the sign of the values.
ruling_note: OQ-09 decided (R10): apply the recommendation in owner-decisions.md OQ-09

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (partial: no validated portfolio basis; a covenant with no stated threshold or a negative current value)
title: An undrawable chart is drawn as 'Source table available...' plus the raw table, not the gap panel, and one covenant row with no threshold removes the bullet chart for every test.
expected: D-14 and CM-021/CM-071: a missing chart is a hatched gap panel with the reason ('unevaluated position stays a gap').
actual: With /connected/portfolio returning {basis: null} (or 404) the Portfolio limits card shows 'Source table available. This report does not record a validated portfolio basis for a chart.' and the full table with its 'Reporting unit' column. With the CP-4 table's first threshold 'Not supplied: not stated', or a negative current value (net cash), the Covenant headroom chart for all three tests is replaced by 'Source table available. The chart could not be drawn on a common basis.' and the table; the two valid rows are not drawn. No GapPanel is used in either state, and the sentences use 'report' and 'basis' in the pipeline sense.
suggested_change: Use GapPanel with a plain reason ('The portfolio limits could not be checked against the mandate for this run').

title: The 'Published model' selector names models 'Model 1 · candidate' using the builder's mode word.
expected: D-16 and CM-019: plain, reader-facing names.
actual: With a second model the select options read 'Model 1 · candidate' and 'Model 2 · alternate'.
suggested_change: Name models by case and date.

title: The 'Compare with the 5% move' control is a select with a single option ('10%').
expected: A control offers a decision (D-35, control matrix: the user can decide exactly what the row says and nothing else); Securities guards with `quotes.length > 2`.
actual: FxShocks draws the select whenever two moves compare; with exactly two moves the only alternative is 10%, so choosing does nothing. Downside.tsx and the rate selector use the same pattern.
suggested_change: Draw the select only when there are two or more alternatives; otherwise state the comparison in the chart subtitle.

title: The same stress case is named 'Downside shock' on the card, chart and comparison table and 'Downside case' in the grid header.
expected: D-26/D-16: one name per case across a screen.
actual: forecastCaseLabel maps 'Downside case' to 'Downside shock' only for cards and the cash proxy chart; the grid group header (and the 'Downside drivers' label for a second downside) keep the stored name.
suggested_change: Apply forecastCaseLabel to the grid's column group labels.
cluster_cause: the stress case is named 'Downside shock' and 'Downside case' on the same report

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (partial: chart amounts in other typographic forms)
title: A chart amount written with a typographic minus, parentheses, a space or no-break space as thousands separator, or a unit suffix removes the whole chart, while Downside reads the typographic minus.
expected: D-31: one unreadable cell should not lose the chart; D-26: one number grammar across components (Downside.position and MacroSensitivity.moneyPosition normalise U+2212).
actual: amount() in visuals/visualData.ts accepts only an ASCII hyphen-minus and comma-grouped digits. With 'Disposal' written '−10' or '(10)', the EBITDA bridge is replaced by 'Source table available. The chart could not be drawn on a common basis.' and the table; the same for the Liquidity bridge with '−450' and for Revenue written '2 100' or '2,100m'. The fallback is safe (no wrong figure is plotted) but the chart is lost; the module text uses U+2212 elsewhere (proof/handoffs/CP-2A.md T2DS.4).
suggested_change: Normalise U+2212 and parenthesised negatives in one shared parser (as Downside already does) and keep rejecting anything else.

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (partial: a model with an 'Upside' or 'Downside (CP-2G drivers)' case)
title: A case whose display name differs from its stored group name shows 'Case description not recorded.' although the model's note for it exists.
expected: CM-065: each forecast case is drawn with its recorded description.
actual: caseDescription builds the note prefix from the display label (`${name} is`), special-casing only 'Downside shock'. With an 'Upside' group and the note 'Upside is the optimistic case...' the card is 'Upside case' with 'Case description not recorded.'; the 'Downside drivers' card behaves the same. The canned run has neither group, so this was reached by rewriting the model in the browser.
suggested_change: Look the note up by the stored group name and show the display label separately.

screen: /report/<run>#calendar (partial: an event name that contains a file name)
title: An event whose name contains a file name is drawn as 'See Evidence', so the reader cannot tell which event it is.
expected: CM-070/D-12: the event is named in words; only the reference is withheld.
actual: eventDisplay replaces the whole cell with 'See Evidence' when containsReference matches, for the date-published, event and relevance columns. With 'Redemption notice per notice_of_redemption.pdf' the row and the Table form read 'See Evidence' and nothing else about the event. Reached by rewriting the event table in the browser.
suggested_change: Strip only the file name ('Redemption notice') or draw the event with its trace control.

title: While the portfolio basis is loading the Portfolio limits card states that the report records no validated basis.
expected: D-31: a loading state is shown as loading; a gap is stated only when the answer is known.
actual: PortfolioBasisProvider supplies null until /connected/portfolio answers, so the card draws 'Source table available. This report does not record a validated portfolio basis for a chart.' and the raw table, then swaps to the chart (3.5 s in the delayed state; one or two frames on a fast local service).
suggested_change: Draw nothing (or a quiet loading line) until the basis request settles.

title: Each Recharts chart is an extra tab stop with role=application, named only by its title, with an empty description.

title: Script check cards are titled "columns", "rows", "all" or "Headroom: all", and draw the service's raw markup, snake_case register names and module codes.

title: The Gaps table prints Markdown marks raw ("**bold**", backticks) and labels every row link "Open source" although it opens the handoff line, not a source.

screen: /report/20261117-072535-01#evidence/summary and #evidence/trace (partial: delivery without zip, handoffs and downloads)

screen: /start step 4, any pathway but Full credit assessment (error)
title: The synthetic test lets the analyst choose, review, approve and submit seven of eight pathways, every one of which ends Failed with "launcher exited 2; see logs/<run>.log".
expected: CT-012 to CT-019: each offered pathway can be run; a failure says what went wrong in words the analyst can act on. Product Principle 2: a limit is a decision the analyst makes, not a line they scroll past.
actual: Lite (5 modules), Deep (20), Earnings Update, Relative Value, Covenant & Refinancing, Distressed & Restructuring and Portfolio Decision were each reviewed, approved and confirmed ('spends USD 0.00'); each run page read 'Failed ... launcher exited 2; see logs/<id>.log' and 0 modules finished. The reason sits in a file the analyst cannot open: 'synthetic proof requires a first Credit Snapshot run' (proof/launcher.py:100). Neither the Purpose step, the review sheet nor the dialog says only Full runs in the synthetic test. The message also shows a server-side path. All seven were submitted in the journey record (Earnings Update only after supplying the two periods it requires, see J1-004); the probe tries Lite and Deep.
suggested_change: State on the Purpose step and the review sheet that the synthetic test runs only the Full credit assessment (do not remove the cards, R5), and put the launcher's own sentence in the run's failure line instead of an exit code and a log path.
verify_note: The failure itself is the synthetic proof's stated limit: docs/react-workflow.md:111-112 tells the user to choose Full credit assessment (Credit Snapshot), and the launcher only runs that pathway. It is not a path a proof user on the documented route meets. What stays a defect is that the page offers, approves and submits the other seven without saying only Full runs in the synthetic test, and that the reason is a server log path. Proof-scoped, so severity lowered.
cause: proof/launcher.py:100 raises 'synthetic proof requires a first Credit Snapshot run'; src/deploy_workflow/inbox/runs.py:355 turns the exit into the path text.
ruling_note: the synthetic proof's documented limit (proof/launcher.py; docs/react-workflow.md tells the user to choose Full with the Northbridge files); what remains is that the page offers and submits other choices without saying so
cluster_cause: the synthetic launcher completes only one run of the Full pathway with the three Northbridge files; every other choice the page offers ends Failed with 'launcher exited 2'

title: Your name is required but unmarked; the first complaint comes at Review run, which returns the analyst to step 1 and resets the stepper to Not started.

The stepper then showed steps 2 to 4 'Not started' although the answers were kept (purpose, agreement and workbook were still set when the analyst went forward again). title: Two files with the same name are kept as two identical rows and refused only at Inspect with 'Choose documents with distinct file names.', which names no file.
expected: The row of a document the page cannot use says which it is and why (control-matrix CT-006; rubric D-16 specific copy); two buttons do not share one accessible name.
actual: Choosing northbridge-filing.txt twice made two identical rows with two identical 'Remove northbridge-filing.txt' buttons and no mark. Nothing happened until Inspect documents, which showed 'Choose documents with distinct file names.'; no row is marked and nothing offers to drop the repeat.
suggested_change: Refuse or mark the repeated name when it is chosen ('Same name as the row above') and name the file in the alert.

title: A second copy of the same document under another name (for example 'northbridge-filing (1).txt') is accepted as a separate document with no flag.
expected: The page lists documents it ignored and why (control-matrix CT-006); a repeated document is called a repeat.
actual: The same filing bytes under two names gave '2 documents inspected, 0 ignored.' with both rows 'unrecognised'; the review sheet's 'Documents read' listed both. Whether a live run would read the filing twice was not verified (R4); in the synthetic test the extra file fails the run (J2-014).
suggested_change: Compare content hashes when files are added and mark a repeat 'Same content as <name>'.

screen: /start, Documents step (error and partial, after Inspect documents)
title: A wrong file type is accepted for upload and described two different ways, and neither says why or which types are read.
expected: The page lists documents it ignored and why (control-matrix CT-006).
actual: A .exe alone gave 'The uploaded documents: no readable issuer file' and stayed 'Selected'; beside a good filing the same file and a .png read 'Ignored / Will not be read' with '1 document inspected, 2 ignored.' The drop zone says only 'Add filings and other source documents. Up to 50 MB per file.'; the file input has no accept list; no text names the types that are read or why a file 'will not be read'.
suggested_change: Name the readable types beside the drop zone and give each ignored row a reason ('Not a document type the run reads').

title: An empty file is reported as 'Empty.txt has no extractable text (scanned image?)': the file name's first letter is capitalised and the hint suggests a scanned image for a 0-byte file.
expected: Copy quotes the file name as it is and says what is wrong (rubric D-16 plain, specific copy).
actual: Choosing empty.txt (0 bytes) alone and inspecting gave 'Empty.txt has no extractable text (scanned image?)'. The row stayed 'Selected'; the analyst's file name is not 'Empty.txt', and a file of 0 bytes is empty, not a scan.
suggested_change: Quote the name unchanged and say 'empty.txt is empty (0 bytes)'; keep the scanned-image hint for files that have bytes and no text.

screen: /start, Review and start after 'Edit purpose and modules' (full)
title: Changing the purpose after approving clears the approval and every limit decision, and the review sheet never says that this happened or why.
expected: Editing after approval invalidates the approval (control-matrix CT-031) and the analyst is told so, so they know why they decide again (PRODUCT.md Principle 2: a limit is a decision the analyst makes).
actual: After approving a Full assessment with three limits accepted (Readiness 'Decisions made 3 of 3', 'Summary approved Met') the analyst pressed 'Edit purpose and modules', chose Lite and returned to Review run. The sheet showed approval unticked, 'Decisions made 0 of 2', Submit disabled and '2 decisions left before you can approve.' Nothing says the earlier approval and decisions were cleared or that the change caused it. The behaviour itself is correct and kept the analyst's note, rating and agreement choice.
suggested_change: Add one sentence at the top of the sheet when a change cleared an approval: 'You changed the purpose, so the approval and your decisions were cleared. Decide again.'

title: A run that stopped offers no retry or resume; its one control, 'Start from this run', opens a new submission and the page does not say so, and the README calls the control something else.
expected: control-matrix CT-038 (resume of an interrupted or capped run: CP-OS resumes, the user relaunches into the same folder, 'no page control found'; an owner matter); apps/issuer-library/README.md ('a failed, capped, rejected or interrupted run's progress view offers "Start again from this run"'); PRODUCT.md Principle 2.
actual: The Failed run page shows a red Failed chip, the reason 'launcher exited 2; see logs/<id>.log' (that log answers 404), 0 of 5 or 14 modules 'Not run', and one header button, 'Start from this run'. No page text says retry, resume, try again or restart. The button opens /start?from=<id>: a new submission with today's date, an empty name and an empty file list until Inspect documents (J1-015). The stopped run stays Failed; the screen does not say that the new run is separate, has its own cap, or whether anything is reused. Why the run failed is J3-002 and J1-003.
suggested_change: Label the control as the README does ('Start again from this run') and add one line saying it begins a new run with its own cap; whether to add a retry or resume control is the owner's decision.
verify_note: The absence of a retry or resume control is an owner matter (CT-038 records 'no page control found'), so that part is not a defect. What is confirmed: the control does not say it starts a new run, and the README calls it 'Start again from this run' (apps/issuer-library/README.md:219). Medium kept for the unexplained new submission; the retry gap itself would be Low.
cause: web/src/pages/connected/RunProgress.tsx:116 labels the control 'Start from this run' and does not say it opens a new, separate submission; src/deploy_workflow/inbox/runs.py:355 reason text.
ruling_note: OQ-06 decided: no resume or retry by design; repair only the wording that 'Start from this run' opens a new submission

title: A Failed run's Activity feed never records that the run stopped: its newest entry still reads 'Running, Run started.'
expected: Run states are shown on the run page (control-matrix CT-035) and what a run could not do is stated, not hidden (PRODUCT.md Positioning).
actual: On the Failed page the chip and a reason box say Failed, but the Activity feed lists only 'Running / Run / Run started.' above 'Queued / Ana L / Run registered.' No entry says the run stopped or why; 'Report' and every module read 'Not run'.
suggested_change: Add a closing feed entry such as 'Run failed' with the reason.

title: Typing an issuer that already has runs shows no notice on Start a run; the earlier runs are looked up only when the analyst presses 'Carry over from latest run'.
expected: apps/issuer-library/README.md 'Starting a run on an issuer': 'The start page also says when a typed issuer ID already has runs (and, if the typed name differs from the filed one, shows the filed name)'.
actual: With one finished run for northbridge-synthetic-group, typing the issuer name by keyboard (the ID followed) and the analyst name, then waiting 2 s, showed no notice and made no request to /api/issuers/<id>. The request was made only when 'Carry over from latest run' was pressed. While a first run was still running, the page also said nothing; only Run activity ('Running 1') showed it. The first warning is the review sheet's 'Changes: Compared with the Full credit assessment run as of 2025-03-31' on step 4.
suggested_change: Look the issuer up when the ID changes and show 'This issuer has N runs, the latest as of <date>' under the field.

screen: /start review sheet then /run/<id> (synthetic test, error, Failed)
title: In the synthetic test, one document more than the three Northbridge files (a re-downloaded copy or any other file) is read, summarised and approved, and the run then ends Failed with no reason the analyst can act on.
expected: A synthetic Submit starts the synthetic engine and spends nothing (control-matrix CT-033); docs/react-workflow.md 'Open the interface' names the files; the sheet itself says 'The synthetic test uses the supplied documents'. A refusal is stated before Submit, not after.
actual: Adding 'northbridge-filing (1).txt' (same bytes) to the three case files gave a review sheet that listed four documents with no warning. Submit ended 'Failed', 0 of 14, 'launcher exited 2; see logs/<id>.log' (the log answers 404). The launcher's own log reads 'synthetic proof requires exactly one northbridge-filing.txt upload and at most its workbook and credit agreement'. A non-duplicate extra file (other-note.txt) failed the same way. Proof-service behaviour only; the live page was not exercised (R4). Same message family as J3-002 and J1-003.
suggested_change: State on the synthetic review sheet which files it accepts, and let the launcher's one-line reason reach the run page (one fix with J3-002).
verify_note: Proof-service behaviour: the synthetic launcher's rule is the documented synthetic limit (docs/react-workflow.md names the files; the sheet says the test uses the supplied documents), so the failure is expected; the defect is only that the sheet does not refuse it before Submit. A user following the docs does not meet it; one who adds a re-downloaded copy does.
cause: proof/launcher.py:26-34 (verify_upload allows exactly the filing plus optional workbook and agreement); no pre-Submit check in the review sheet.
ruling_note: the synthetic proof's documented limit (proof/launcher.py; docs/react-workflow.md tells the user to choose Full with the Northbridge files); what remains is that the page offers and submits other choices without saying so

screen: /runs and /run/<id> (partial, a run waiting behind three running)
title: A run that waits behind three running ones is listed under Waiting and shown as Queued with no reason, no limit and no position.
expected: apps/issuer-library/README.md 'Waiting runs': a run waits when 3 are going; Run activity lists it under Waiting and says why; status changes are explained (rubric D-43).
actual: Four runs confirmed within 0.6 s gave 'Running 3, Waiting 1'. The Waiting table has two columns (Issuer, Pathway); the run's own page says 'Queued', 'Elapsed n.a. not available', 'No start time recorded'. Nothing says three runs are going, that this is a limit, or what it waits for, so a waiting run cannot be told from a stuck one. It did start when one of the three ended (about 5 s) and finished.
suggested_change: Add one reason line to the Waiting row and the run page: 'Waiting: 3 runs are going (the limit). It starts when one ends.'

screen: /report/<id> opened while the run is still going (error)
title: The report address of a run that is still going says 'The published report could not be loaded.' and not that the run is still running.
expected: Loading, empty and error states are designed and say what is true (rubric D-31).
actual: Opening /report/<id> 0.8 s after Submit gave 'Credit report / The published report could not be loaded.' (the service answered 404 'unknown report' for /connected/snapshot?run=<id>, one console error). The same address loaded the full report once the run had ended. The 'Open report' link appears only after publication, so the analyst meets this through a copied or bookmarked address, which is how a person returns after leaving.
suggested_change: When the run is not finished, show 'This run is still going' with a link to its Run activity page.

title: Overview lists 13 modules under 'Bottom line by module' while the tab says 'Modules 14'; the headline Bottom line and Key findings come from 'Committee decision', which is named only inside the trace drawer and the Limitations list.
expected: Reader standard (docs/rulings/2026-11-11-reader-and-issuer-report.md via AGENTS.md:30-37): the reader should not have to guess which module a judgement comes from; two counts on one screen should agree or say why.
actual: Tab bar 'Modules 14'; the module list has 13 rows and no Committee decision row; the band 'Bottom line: The synthetic issuer shows one observed item.' and the card 'The synthetic issuer's cover is thin at 3.1x.' name no author. Only the drawers say 'Committee decision · Handoff line 28 / 32'. The Committee decision page's own verdict ('Final Sizing Posture: Requires More Work') is not on Overview. The finding's drawer offers only Close and Open in Evidence; no control takes the reader from a finding to the module page that wrote it.
probe: journey.md step 2 (observed; a probe is required only from Medium)
suggested_change: Label the headline band and each key finding with its author module as a link, and either add the 14th row or say 'Bottom line by module (13 of 14; the committee decision is above)'.

title: The left rail's two icon links (a book, a play button) have no visible label and no tooltip, so a first-time reader must guess that they mean Library and Run activity.
expected: Reader who 'has not read the source documents' (PRODUCT.md:11); icon-only navigation needs a label or tooltip.
actual: Accessible names exist ('Library', 'Run') but nothing is drawn: no text, no title attribute, and hovering the play icon for 1.2 s showed only a grey hover tint, no tooltip. The accessible name 'Run' also differs from the page it opens, 'Run activity'.
probe: journey.md step 8 (observed; a probe is required only from Medium)
suggested_change: Add a tooltip (and a visible label at widths that allow) and use 'Run activity' as the name.

title: Overview's key finding says 'cover is thin at 3.1x' directly beside a tile 'Interest coverage 4.00x +0.80x vs FY2023 better', and never says which cover measure 3.1x is.
expected: Exact values with their quantity family (AGENTS.md:65): two different covers on one screen need names.
actual: Key findings: 'The synthetic issuer's cover is thin at 3.1x.' Tile: 'Interest coverage 4.00x, better'. The Downside module calls 3.10 'All-in cover (x)' for the control case; Financial foundation's chart shows interest cover 3.20 (FY2023) and 4.00 (FY2024). A reader sees 'thin' next to 'better' with no explanation.
probe: journey.md step 2 (observed; a probe is required only from Medium)

title: 'Dates to watch' and the Issuer calendar use unexplained words ('Wall', 'Cost', 'Rating', '· day', '· month') and show a 'Historical' event dated after the as-of date and a 'Scheduled' event on the as-of date.
expected: Reader who has not read the sources (PRODUCT.md:11); labels need to be understandable without the handoff.
actual: Rows read 'Synthetic note / Source readiness · Wall / Scheduled — matures / 2025-03-31 · day'; the calendar has a 2025-06 event labelled Historical when the case date is 2025-03-31, and the same four events repeat for nine modules (36 events). Nothing explains 'Wall' (maturity wall) or the precision words. Most of this is canned proof content; the unexplained vocabulary is not.
probe: journey.md step 2 (observed; a probe is required only from Medium)
suggested_change: Spell out 'Maturity wall', drop the precision words or show them as a date format, and explain Historical against the as-of date.

title: Evidence > Script checks shows a badge '215' and a list in which 205 items read 'not checked', with no sentence saying what a script check is or what 'not checked' means.
expected: PRODUCT.md:23 (state limits explicitly); a count in a tab badge needs a definition for a reader who has not read the sources.
actual: Rows such as 'Legal & covenants 32 not checked', 'Security selection 1 agreed 35 not checked'. Totals: 9 agreed, 1 noted, 205 not checked. A reader can take this as 95% of the run's numbers being unverified, or as noise; the page does not say which.
probe: journey.md step 7 (observed; a probe is required only from Medium)

title: Opening Evidence from the Forecast Revenue chart lands on a block that prints a literal '```json' fence and a single-line machine-readable JSON object.
expected: Owner design rule 'nothing may look extracted from Markdown' (PRODUCT.md:46); Evidence may show machinery but not the Markdown fence characters.

title: The forecast case is called 'Downside shock' on its card and comparison row but 'Downside case' on the cash flow table and the notes, and the Downside module calls its scenarios 'Cost shock' and 'Cost and rate shock'.
expected: One name per thing across screens (harmony rubric; control-matrix CT-045 'Choosing a forecast case').
actual: Card: 'Downside shock 97.47'. After choosing it the table header reads 'Line item | Downside case'; note 'Downside case is the stress case: a shock applied to the base-case drivers.'

title: 'Confidence score 89 High' appears on every module page with no scale, no definition and no sentence next to it; its trace drawer repeats 'no page / the row cites no page or register' fourteen times.
expected: PRODUCT.md:11 (reader has not read the sources) and principle 3 (findings on working pages, machinery on Evidence); a score needs its scale.

The card's trace control is named 'Show sources for this figure'; the drawer's statement is 'Confidence inputs' (Handoff line 161) followed by 14 identical 'no page / the row cites no page or register' rows. The inputs list (Directly Sourced 8, Calculated 2, ..., Fields present 95 of 100, Source gate pass) is inside a disclosure further down; nothing says how 89 follows or what 100 would mean.

title: The Downside module formats the same quantity two ways ('EBITDA decline 0.1 (10%)' and 'FCF reaches zero 0.10 (10%)') and labels a drop-down 'Compare with Control (unstressed)' while it shows 'Cost shock'.

title: The tab named 'Report' opens a page titled 'Report history', the breadcrumb reads 'Library / Report' with 'Report' not a link, and the library card link '1 run' goes to the same page; a reader has to guess that 'Report' means the run history.

title: The header switch 'Show sources' only draws a ring around the existing trace icons; it shows no source, which is what its name promises.

screen: /report/<run>#overview, #modules/CP-4, CP-2A, CP-1, CP-3C, CP-0 and #forecast, full
title: The finished synthetic run shows different values for the same measure on different screens, and nothing states a definition, a period or a reason for the difference.
expected: A measure shows one value, or each value carries its definition, period and basis: PRODUCT.md Positioning ('what a run could not do is stated, not hidden'), AGENTS.md ('Preserve values, periods, units, source references, limitations and analytical conclusions'); the Evidence validation module exists to cross-check modules.
actual: Interest cover: Overview tile 4.00x (FY2024), Key findings claim 3.1x, Legal & covenants current 2.6x, Downside control all-in cover 3.10x. Net leverage: Overview tile 2.25x (FY2024), Legal & covenants current 4.2x, Downside control 1.25x, Forecast FY2025E 1.23x. The USD 1,250m maturity that the contrary-evidence claim rests on falls in FY2028 in Financial foundation (FY2027 'Not supplied: the schedule stops here') and in FY2027 in Refinancing & LME; the analyst's own run note says 'Check the 2028 maturities'. Source readiness says 'Only the synthetic filing is available' and 'Financing terms are absent' while the run holds the filing, an executed agreement and a workbook. Also: EBITDA FY2023 is 400 (T4.4), 410 'Adjusted' (chart) and 410 'Reported' with 430 adjusted (bridge); the Forecast base year (revenue 1,000, debt 600, cash 100) is not the reported FY2024 (2,250, 1,400, 275); the Downside module shocks EBITDA by 10% or 20% with cash interest unchanged or +5%, the Forecast by 20% with rates +10%; the Debt stack adds to 2,000 (4.0x cumulative) against total debt of 1,400 (2.80x); a Minimum liquidity covenant of 100 US$m is shown that the agreement (Sections 1 and 2 only) does not contain. Twelve modules' Contrary evidence sections all say 'Nothing supplied contradicts the view'. The cause is the canned handoffs in proof/handoffs/, which contradict one another; no screen flags any of it.
suggested_change: Make the canned handoffs agree (one cover and one net leverage with a stated basis, one maturity year, a CP-0 that matches the three uploaded files, one downside definition) so the proof is a coherent demonstration. Whether the library should show unreconciled values across modules is the owner's decision, because delivery adds no analysis.
verify_note: The differences come from the canned handoffs under proof/handoffs/, which contradict one another; I found each value in the handoff text and the page shows it unchanged, with no period or unit altered by delivery. Module-written content that delivery must not change; not a delivery defect.
cause: proof/handoffs/CP-1A.md:9, CP-2A.md:94, CP-1.md:34 and CP-3C.md:25, CP-2G.md:78 - the canned handoffs state these values.
cluster_cause: the same measure shows different values or names on different screens with no basis, period or reason stated

title: The Confidence score (89, High) is right but its method is shown nowhere, and its trace drawer lists fourteen 'the row cites no page or register' lines.
expected: A derived figure shows how it was derived: AGENTS.md reader standard ('every paragraph, row and figure traces'); the module's own method is fixed by ruling (matrix CT-049) but must be visible to be checked; docs/rulings/2026-11-11-reader-and-issuer-report.md.
actual: Every module page shows 'Confidence score 89 High' (all 14 handoffs carry the same inputs). The drawer repeats 'no page / the row cites no page or register' fourteen times for the inputs table and gives no weights, source-gate factor, coverage share or penalty. Recomputed by hand from the table (lineage 8 / 2 / 2, weights 1.0 / 0.9 / 0.5, evidence 90; fields 95 of 100; gate pass; one minor finding at 3 points): (0.6 x 90 + 0.4 x 95) - 3 = 89, so the value is right; the person cannot do this from the screen.
suggested_change: State the method in the score's drawer (the lineage weights, the 60/40 split between evidence and field coverage, the gate factor and the penalties) and replace the fourteen 'no page' lines with the inputs table itself.
verify_note: Content matrix CM-080 says the score is computed by Python from the inputs table and that table is audit material shown on Evidence > Record; the tile with a trace to the inputs is the designed form and the value is right. The 14 repeated 'cites no page' lines are polish, not misleading.
cause: web/src/pages/connected/report/Confidence.tsx:6-40 - the tile traces to the handoff's Confidence inputs table; method lives in src/deploy_workflow/confidence.py:15.

title: The issuer calendar counts one dated event once per module that repeats it, and the Overview's Dates to watch lists one event five times.
expected: The count in a chart header equals the number of distinct events the chart draws, and a reader who has not read the sources is not told of events that are one event repeated (AGENTS.md reader standard; PRODUCT.md principle 4, exact values survive every boundary).
actual: The calendar header says 'Historical 9, Scheduled 18, Scenario 9' (36 events). The 14 handoffs carry 36 event rows for 4 distinct events (2025-03-31 Synthetic note, 2025-06 Synthetic call, 2025-Q3 Synthetic review, 2026 Synthetic maturity), each repeated by nine modules and listed nine times with the module's name. The Overview's Dates to watch shows the 2025-03-31 'Synthetic note' five times. In a real run, several modules citing the same maturity would inflate the counts the same way.
suggested_change: Merge rows with the same date, event and status into one row that lists the modules that reported it, and count merged events.
verify_note: Each row is one module's recorded event with its owner and source, which is the page's stated per-module design; merging events across modules would be delivery making an analytical judgement. The repetition comes from the canned handoffs carrying the same four events in nine modules. A cross-module dedup is an owner design choice.
cause: web/src/pages/connected/report/Calendar.tsx:61-95 - rows are built per module with the owner name and a per-row source link; no cross-module merge.

title: The rating's as-of date (2025-02-28) is only in a hover title on a non-focusable element, so it is not visible on a touch screen or by keyboard.
expected: Information is available without a pointer: PRODUCT.md Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA working assumption). The analyst entered the date at run start and the card is the only place the rating is shown.
actual: The card reads 'Moody's B1 Negative / Entered at run start'. The date exists only as title='as of 2025-02-28' on the list item (no tabindex); the date appears in no visible text on the Overview, Evidence or Run record.
suggested_change: Print the as-of date (and scope) in the card's text.
ruling_note: R14 (owner, 2026-11-17: 'only pc, no need for keyboard'): the app runs on desktop PCs with a mouse; narrow-screen, touch and keyboard-only findings are not defects; any reviewed fix already merged stays

title: The Forecast page prose names module codes (CP-1, CP-2G) and says 'Python's arithmetic'.

title: Several trace controls on one page share the same accessible name, so a screen-reader user cannot tell which row or passage each opens.
expected: A control's name says what it acts on (WCAG 2.2 2.4.6; PRODUCT.md Accessibility).
actual: Overview: 'Show sources for this passage' x2 (Key findings and Contrary evidence). Forecast: 'Show sources for Cash proxy by scenario' x3. Financial foundation: 'Show sources for FY2024' x2 (Net debt data and Debt principal rows).
suggested_change: Name row controls with the table and the row ('Net debt data, FY2024') and passage controls with their section heading.

title: The Script checks tab shows 215 although 205 of the checks did not run.
expected: A count on a tab reflects what the reader will find under it: reader standard in AGENTS.md; what a run could not do is stated, not hidden (PRODUCT.md).
actual: The badge reads 215. By module the page shows 205 'not checked', 9 'agreed' and 1 'noted'. A reader taking 215 as checks passed is misled; the per-module lines are accurate.

title: The same measure carries different names on different screens, and similar names stand for different measures.
expected: One name per measure across the library, so a reader can follow a figure from the Overview to the module and the Forecast (harmony rule; AGENTS.md reader standard).
actual: Debt over EBITDA is 'Gross leverage' on the Overview, 'Total debt / EBITDA' on Financial foundation and 'Total leverage (debt / Adj EBITDA)' on the Forecast. EBITDA over cash interest is 'Interest coverage' on the Overview, 'Interest cover' on Financial foundation and Legal & covenants, and 'Interest coverage (Adj EBITDA / interest)' on the Forecast, while the Downside module's 'All-in cover (x)' is a different measure.
