actual: strOrNull and Figure.value accept '': Spend and Elapsed draw empty big figures and the Confirm row 'Name' an empty value cell. The probe reads the figure cells as ['', '5 of 13', ''].
suggested_change: Treat a blank string as missing: reject it in the reader or draw <Missing /> for it.

title: Text is drawn below 13 px in six places: 12 px captions, step notes, times, module chips and the upload hint, and 9 px on the file-type label.
expected: D-30 (nothing written here below 13 px; caption 13/18). The config.json exceptions cover one mockup file only.
actual: text-xs (12 px): Stepper note, Summary caption, Feed time, Purpose module chip, Documents upload hint; text-[9px] on the PDF and XLSX label of each file row. Probe lists 15 distinct strings on five pages.
suggested_change: Use the caption token (13/18) for these, and keep the file-type label inside the icon at 13 px or draw it as an icon.

title: Spacing and sizes off the 4/8/12/16/20/24/32 ladder: gap-7 (28 px) between Confirm groups, 6 px and 2 px gaps, and fixed 38 px, 27 px, 18 px and 9 px values on the file icon and alert rings.
expected: D-26 (spacing steps from the ladder; no p-[13px]-style literals); D-30.
actual: Confirm.tsx gap-7; gap-1.5, pt-1.5 and mt-1.5 in ModuleSteps, Context and Documents; mt-0.5 and gap-0.5; Documents.tsx h-[38px] w-[27px] left-[7px] top-[18px] rounded-[2px] text-[9px]; RunAlert after:size-[38px].
suggested_change: Use ladder steps (gap-8, gap-2) and tokenise the file-icon and ring sizes.

title: The Readiness panel nests three bordered surfaces and its item boxes have the same radius as the panel around them.
expected: D-21 (no cards inside cards; every list item in its own bordered box is the failing example); D-23 (a nested element has a smaller radius than its container).
actual: Measured: aside 28 px radius with shadow, ItemGroup section 20 px (surface-subtle), each item 20 px with its own border. The connected StartReadiness draws the same facts as hairline-divided rows (no nested boxes), so the two surfaces also differ (D-26).
suggested_change: Draw the items as rows divided by hairlines, as the connected panel does, and reuse one component.

title: The same FileCheck02 featured icon is drawn on every purpose card; it says nothing the title does not.
expected: D-20 (no decorative icons that carry no meaning; an icon beside every item is the failing pattern).
actual: Each of the four (connected: eight) cards starts with an identical 'brand' featured icon plus the title.
suggested_change: Drop the repeated icon, or use it only on the selected card.
cluster_cause: every purpose card carries the same FileCheck icon (Purpose.tsx, drawn on both surfaces)

title: The upload hint lists PDF, DOCX, HTML or XLSX; the reader also accepts CSV, TXT, MD, JSON and JSONL, and the connected page names no types.
expected: CT-006 (Excel and CSV files are inputs); src/deploy_workflow/owners/cpos_launch.py SOURCE_SUFFIXES (.pdf .htm .html .docx .txt .md .xlsx .csv .json .jsonl).
actual: Documents.tsx hard-codes 'PDF, DOCX, HTML or XLSX, up to 50 MB each'; a CSV an analyst is allowed to upload is not named.
suggested_change: Say 'Up to 50 MB per file' as the connected page does, or list every accepted type.

title: On the shipped build every run page is the single line 'No run data in this library': no sentence says why or what to do, and the link to start a run is absent.
expected: D-31 (empty state: featured icon, title, one sentence and where it exists the next action); CM-036 (activity with no runs says so).
actual: All 22 addresses show the featured icon and one heading; the fixture variant of the same case ('No run to watch') has a sentence and a 'Start a run' button.
suggested_change: Add one sentence ('This library holds no run records') and a link to the Library.

title: The Documents step cannot be completed: Next says 'Replace or remove the unreadable file to continue', while Replace file, Remove and the drop zone (which still reads 'or drag and drop') are all disabled.
expected: CT-006 (the user adds, removes or carries documents); a reason that tells the reader to act must name an action that exists.
actual: All nine file controls are disabled; the reason text is a visible line below the drop zone. The drop zone has no drop handler, so dropping a file on the page falls to the browser's default (not exercised, see Not verified).
suggested_change: Say in the Next reason that the page is a saved example, and drop the words 'or drag and drop' while the zone is inert.

screen: #/run/start/* after Next or Previous at 390 px (full, fixture)
title: Moving to another step keeps the previous scroll offset: at 390 px the new step opens with its heading 326 px above the viewport.
expected: D-22 (the first thing on a screen is the first thing seen); WCAG 2.4.3 (focus order after a view change).
actual: On Confirm, scrolled to its end, 'Approve summary' lands on More context with main.scrollTop 635 and the h2 at y = -326; focus stays on the Next link. At 1440 px the offset resets only because the page is short.
suggested_change: Scroll main to the top and move focus to the step heading when the draft changes (the root cause may be the shell's main region, S1).
ruling_note: R14 (owner, 2026-11-17: 'only pc, no need for keyboard'): the app runs on desktop PCs with a mouse; narrow-screen, touch and keyboard-only findings are not defects; any reviewed fix already merged stays

title: An unreadable file row carries two Remove controls: the icon (named 'Remove <file>') and a text button named only 'Remove'.
expected: D-37 (no two different actions share a generic name; a name says what it removes).
actual: Accessibility tree: button 'Remove Investor presentation, scanned.pdf' and button 'Remove'. Both are disabled, so the pair is not heard in a tab walk, but a screen-reader list of buttons names one generically.
suggested_change: Give the text button the file name (aria-label) or drop the duplicate.

title: Disabled controls are unfocusable, so the reason attached to them with aria-describedby is never reached by Tab.
expected: D-35 (everything is operable and discoverable from the keyboard); D-37.
actual: Tab walk of #/run/start/documents stops at Skip, the rail and Library only: Click to upload, every Remove, Previous and Next are skipped. Stop run on the live pages is skipped the same way. The reason is visible text beside the control, so it is reachable in reading mode.
suggested_change: Use aria-disabled with a focusable button that announces the reason, or place the reason where reading order meets it first.
ruling_note: R14 (owner, 2026-11-17: 'only pc, no need for keyboard'): the app runs on desktop PCs with a mouse; narrow-screen, touch and keyboard-only findings are not defects; any reviewed fix already merged stays

title: The saved example contradicts itself: the More context textarea is empty but the Start recap says 'One note added'; 'a library appears under TransDigm Group' when the library holds no such issuer; the intro line says 'Nothing is spent before the last step' on the page that follows it.
expected: D-15 (the same figure and fact read the same across a flow); CM-086.
actual: Context draft note is '' while the Start recap row is 'More context: One note added'. Started text: 'its library appears under TransDigm Group when it finishes'. The intro paragraph stays on Run started.
suggested_change: Make the fixture consistent and hide the intro line once the run has started.

screen: #/kit (shipped, 1440 and 390 px); every page that draws a MetricCard, Timeline, Table, chart tick or label
title: Text that the project wrote itself is set at 12 px and 10 px, under the 13 px floor.
expected: D-30: nothing written here is set below 13 px (caption 13/18); a column header is caption 13/18 text-tertiary (D-30 Pass). Source components keep their source's sizes, so only pieces written here are counted.
actual: The scan of #/kit finds 12 px text in MetricCard's 'from' figure (MetricCard.tsx:41), the Timeline date (Timeline.tsx:43), the Table column headings (table.tsx:118), all chart axis ticks and labels (TICK 12 in TrendChart, and fontSize 12 in SeriesLine, WaterfallChart, ColumnsChart, PathChart, ScatterPlot; text-xs in LimitsChart) and 10 px in the ProgressSteps numerals (ProgressSteps.tsx:49). Same measurement at 1440 and 390 px. The rail labels are Shell code and are in S1-014; the Badge sm, Tooltip and file-upload hint are source components at 12 px and are not counted.
suggested_change: Set the written-here pieces to the caption token (13 px) or larger, including chart tick fonts; decide separately whether the source-sized pieces (Table head, Badge sm, Tooltip) take the caption size too.
cluster_cause: text set below the 13 px floor in project-written components and pages

screen: #/kit, Empty state; every page that draws EmptyState.Title (run start Documents, run activity, library and model empty states)
title: The empty-state title is set in Geist, not in the heading face.
expected: D-30: headings are Schibsted Grotesk 600 or 700 (font-display); Geist is for body, interface and figures.
actual: EmptyState.Title is an h2 or h3 with 'text-xl font-semibold text-primary' and no font-display; the scan reads its computed family as Geist, 20 px, while all 50 other headings on #/kit are Schibsted Grotesk.
suggested_change: Add font-display (and the h3 size token) to EmptyState.Title.

title: Three different cards draw a headline figure: the kit MetricCard, the library MetricTile and the model MetricTile.
expected: D-26 (sibling screens agree on type size, radius, padding) and D-23 (radius from the ladder 6/12/20/28); the design system gives one metric card per metric and a metric type token of 40/44 (design-system.md:242, :317).
actual: Measured in the fixture: MetricCard (used by PairTile and the kit) figure 24 px, radius 8 px, padding 24, no shadow; library MetricTile figure 30 px, radius 12, padding 20, shadow; model MetricTile figure 28 px, radius 28, padding 20, shadow, hairline border. None uses the 40 px metric token, and 8 px is not on the radius ladder. Each tile comment says the kit MetricCard 'has no place' for what it needs, so the tiles were rebuilt.
suggested_change: Pick one headline-figure card (figure size, radius, padding, shadow) and make the other two compose it, giving the MetricCard slots for a trace control, a gap and a delta line.

screen: Table.Cell in any table (checked in a component bundle; used on #/library/home list and the connected Run activity tables)
title: A table cell draws n.a. only for null; an undefined or empty-string cell is drawn blank.
expected: D-14: a missing figure is the text 'n.a.' in text-tertiary, never a blank cell. The doc comment on TableCell says 'a null child is a figure that is missing'.
actual: With four rows whose figure is null, undefined, '' and '0', the cells read 'n.a. (not available)', blank, blank and '0'. The test is children === null. The prop type is ReactNode, so undefined and '' type-check. One live caller can already pass an empty value: RunActivity draws {run.reason} in the Reason column.
suggested_change: Treat undefined like null in TableCell (or narrow the children type so undefined and '' fail the type check); keep a blank cell only where a column means 'no value' and say so.
cluster_cause: a table cell draws n.a. only for null; an empty string draws blank

screen: #/library/halden-aerostructures/2026-09-30/modules/business-profile (static fixture, contrary evidence); every Alert with tone warning or error
title: Every warning or error Alert is role=alert, including the permanent 'Contrary evidence' passage on each module page.
expected: D-43: role=alert is for errors that need action; a static passage is not a live announcement. D-03 draws contrary evidence as the warning-toned Alert, so it must be possible to draw that passage without an assertive live role.
actual: Alert.tsx maps warning and error to role='alert' with no prop to change it. On the fixture Modules page the contrary-evidence passage is a role=alert region (with an sr-only 'Warning:' prefix), so it is exposed as an interrupting announcement when the page renders. Not tried with a screen reader.
suggested_change: Give Alert a prop (or a static variant) that drops the live role for a passage that is part of the page, and keep role=alert for errors raised after load.
ruling_note: R16 (owner, 2026-11-17: 'screen reader - not required'): a finding that changes only what a screen reader announces is not a defect; any reviewed fix already merged stays

screen: Every chart (checked on #/kit Trend chart, 1440 px); charts also on #/model/* and the connected Forecast tab
title: Each chart drawing is exposed as an application widget named only by its title, with no description and no stated kind.
expected: D-44 and D-37: every chart has a name and a short description (kind of chart and what it shows); the table form is the full alternative.
actual: The Recharts svg has role='application', tabindex=0, no aria-label, no aria-describedby and an empty desc; its name is the title plus the tick text ('Debt by period FY21 FY22 ... 600'). ChartFrame links a description only when a subtitle is given, and TrendChart passes none. Each chart adds a tab stop; ArrowRight moves the tooltip, so keyboard reading of values works. The Chart or Table toggle remains the full alternative.
suggested_change: Give the drawing role=img with a label that says the chart kind and what it shows (or pass the subtitle through for every chart), and keep the table toggle as the full reading.

title: A hovered, unselected tab is drawn exactly like the selected tab.
expected: D-39 (the selected tab is told by a 2 px line as well as colour) and D-27 (hover tints a neutral surface). D-08 (source look) says the tab keeps its source's states.
actual: Tabs.tsx applies 'border-fg-brand-primary_alt text-brand-secondary' for (isSelected || isHovered). Hovering 'Changes' gives it the same blue 2 px underline and blue text as the selected 'Overview', so two tabs read as selected while the pointer rests on one. Same computed colours (underline rgb(0,26,255), text rgb(0,26,255)).
suggested_change: Draw hover as the text colour change alone (no line), keeping the line for the selected tab; this departs from the source look, so the owner chooses between D-08 and D-27.
ruling_note: OQ-09 decided (R10): apply the recommendation in owner-decisions.md OQ-09

screen: Connected /run/<id> (Run progress): Modules and Activity cards; static #/run/activity/:run twin
title: Card draws its title as an h3 with no way to set the level, so the connected Run progress page goes from h1 to h3.
expected: D-36: headings in order with no skipped level; static and connected twins agree (D-26).
actual: Card.tsx always renders <h3>. RunProgress.tsx:154 and :165 put Card title='Modules' and Card title='Activity' directly under the page h1, with no h2 in the page code between them. The static twin (ActivityPage.tsx:121) draws the same two headings as h2. Read from the code and a component render (h1, h3); the connected page itself was not opened.
suggested_change: Add an 'as' prop to Card (as Timeline and ChartFrame have) and pass h2 from RunProgress.

title: The kit's paid-run sample dialog tells the reader the run 'stops at the cap of USD 20' with no pathway named.
expected: Retired R-09: no flat USD 20 cap; the cap is Lite 15, Full 25, Deep 40 and 20 for the five purpose pathways (docs/rulings/2026-11-15-pathway-tiers-and-caps.md).
actual: Kit7e.tsx:76 reads 'This run costs money and cannot be undone. It stops at the cap of USD 20.' beside a Start the run button, on a page the static rail offers. It is sample copy, but it states one cap for any run. (File owned by S1; the matrix row is the retired list.)
suggested_change: Name a pathway and its cap in the sample ('It stops at the Full cap of USD 25'), or drop the figure.

screen: ColumnsChart, StackChart, RangeStripChart and WaterfallChart (kit-free; checked in a component bundle and on the fixture Forecast page)
title: Bar, stack and strip series are told apart by colour alone, and the first and third chart colours are almost the same grey.
expected: D-39 and D-28: series differ by more than hue (a legend with colour swatches only is a signal); the chart survives a grayscale conversion, as the line charts do with dash and marker.
actual: Lines carry a dash and a marker (series.ts); bars, stack segments and strip ticks do not. BarLegend and RankedLegend draw plain colour squares. In grey, chart-1 (#001aff, luminance 0.080) and chart-3 (#994a34, 0.119) differ by a ratio of 1.31, so the first and third bar of a group are hard to tell apart in a grayscale print (the grayscale capture shows Term loan and Revolver as near-identical dark bars); the waterfall total and down colours are the same pair (1.31), though its labels carry a sign. The fixed order of the bars in each group is the only second cue.
suggested_change: Give the legend and the bars a second cue (a pattern, or the series name drawn once over the first group), or separate the lightness of the first three chart tokens; the palette is the design system's, so the owner chooses.
ruling_note: OQ-09 decided (R10): apply the recommendation in owner-decisions.md OQ-09

screen: PathChart (forecast cases; every page that draws it), checked at 1440 px
title: Each path chart has a focusable 'scroll horizontally' region that does not scroll, in addition to the chart's own tab stop.
expected: D-35: a tab stop does something; D-37: a name says what the control does. A region is focusable only where it can scroll.
actual: PathChart wraps the chart in a div role=region, tabIndex=0, aria-label '<title> chart; scroll horizontally to read each period', at every width. At 1440 px its scrollWidth equals its clientWidth (344 and 344), so the stop has no effect, and a screen reader is told to scroll where nothing scrolls. The Recharts svg inside it is a second tab stop (role=application), so every path chart costs two stops. The jsx-a11y rule no-noninteractive-tabindex is switched off on that line.
suggested_change: Make the region focusable only when its content overflows (a resize check), or drop the wrapper's tab stop and keep the svg's.
ruling_note: R14 (owner, 2026-11-17: 'only pc, no need for keyboard'): the app runs on desktop PCs with a mouse; narrow-screen, touch and keyboard-only findings are not defects; any reviewed fix already merged stays

screen: #/model/transdigm/2025-06-30/forecast (static fixture), 'What drives each case', row 'Aftermarket share of revenue'
title: A range strip row with no range draws neither the strip nor the two case markers, and no n.a. in the track, although both case values are delivered.
expected: D-14: a missing item leaves a gap marked n.a., and a present value is drawn. The row delivers positions 55 and 52 on an axis 0 to 100 and their texts.
actual: Track returns null when range is null, so the markers are not drawn: the track cell is empty (no strip, no marker, no n.a.), while the value column shows '55%' and '52%' with their colour ticks and the label says 'Range n.a.'. The note under the chart explains only the missing strip. The other missing case, 'Working capital days', keeps its strip and writes n.a. twice in the value column.
suggested_change: Draw the markers when the range is null (they have their own positions on the axis) and write n.a. in the track where nothing is drawn.

title: The gate test:file:gates exits 1 in the cloud container because its default browser hangs on every page.
expected: The gate exits 0 on a clean tree (docs/QUALITY-GATE.md; web/package.json script test:file:gates).
actual: Exit 1 in 5 of 5 tries; the page check times out. With CHROME_PATH set to the installed headless shell and CI=true the same gate exits 0 with 134 PASS (baseline row 8b).
suggested_change: none: the cause is the container's browser wrapper; check the gate once on the work PC
ruling_note: environment cause in the cloud container (baseline row 8b passes with a working browser); check once on the work PC

title: The run root is limited to 80 characters; a longer path is refused at start.

ruling_note: a deliberate guard with a clear message (layout.py:61); named in the work-PC prompt

title: The service serves routes the connected client never calls: GET /connected/reports, GET /api/runs/<id>, GET /activity.js, /data.js, /assets/*, /THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, /index.html and /library/index.html.

ruling_note: R17 (owner, 2026-11-17: 'agreed'): both legacy pages stay for this hand-over; the connected app depends on the legacy library's build (library/data.js and library/downloads, written by apps/issuer-library/update_library.py), and Python context checks and five test files rely on the legacy form; separating the data build from the old page, and moving the form's rules into Python, is work after the audit

title: The scheduler posts run cards to a Teams webhook when CREDIT_OS_TEAMS_WEBHOOK and CREDIT_OS_TEAMS_LINK are set, a request to another host that README ruling R8 does not list as an exception; proof.serve does not clear the two variables.
expected: README ruling R8: the application works entirely offline, with CP-DR's lookups during a live run as the one recorded exception. docs/rulings/2026-11-16-teams-run-cards.md records Teams as a second exception, as one session's reading of the owner's answer.
actual: src/deploy_workflow/inbox/teams.py:182-197 posts with urllib when both variables are set; proof/serve.py:22-32 clears provider keys but not the Teams variables, so a synthetic run can post a card for a synthetic run.
suggested_change: none: the owner confirms or withdraws the Teams exception to R8, and says whether proof.serve clears the two variables
verify_note: The claim that a synthetic run can post is wrong: proof.serve passes launcher=launcher_command(), so Settings(root, launcher=...) has teams=None (scheduler.py:73,168-169), the variables are never read, and the launched child drops the webhook (runs.py:126). The Teams post on the regular service is the recorded exception to R8 (README R8/R10, docs/rulings/2026-11-16-teams-run-cards.md). R8's 'must clear both' is met in effect, though proof/serve.py does not clear them explicitly; a one-line pop would only make that visible.
ruling_note: OQ-11 decided (R10): the Teams exception is recorded in R8; not a defect in proof.serve: a synthetic service builds its scheduler without Teams settings (react_frontend/__init__.py:399-403), so it never posts

title: The library index sends 43 KB for one run, almost all of it fields the page never reads (artifacts, files, gaps, summary, workflow, country, currency).
expected: Stage 6 measure: a list page asks for the fields it draws. LibraryIndex and HeadlineFigures read id, name, issuer, title, date, sector, period and metrics only.
actual: GET /connected/library for one finished run returned 43,351 bytes: catalogue.real[0] carries artifacts[] and files[] with delivery paths and file names, gaps, summary and more (react_frontend/__init__.py:97-116 keeps the whole catalogue entry). The page is re-fetched on each visit (cache: no-store).
suggested_change: Project catalogue.real to the eight fields the page draws, as _library_index already does for workspace.runs.

screen: ConnectedApp routing: /start/, /runs/, unknown address; ReportReader 'no report' branch
title: Several client branches cannot be reached through the service: trailing-slash /start/ and /runs/, the 'Page not found' page, and 'No report was published for this run.'
expected: Code check: no branch that no input reaches. The service's own page list (_app_page, react_frontend/__init__.py:235-243) is what decides which addresses reach the client.
actual: ConnectedApp matches path === '/start/' and '/runs/' (ConnectedApp.tsx:64,66) but the service answers GET /start/ and GET /runs/ with 404 {"error":"not found"} (it serves /run/<id>/ and /report/<id>/ with a trailing slash only). The Page-not-found PageHeader (ConnectedApp.tsx:82) is reached by no address the service serves; the browser shows the JSON 404 instead. ReaderStatus's 'No report was published for this run.' (ReportLibrary.tsx:424-426) is unreachable because the service answers 404 for an unknown folder and getSnapshot throws. ConnectedLoadBoundary's `reload` prop and ConnectedApp's `navigate`/`search` props are test seams no production caller passes.
suggested_change: Either serve the trailing-slash forms and a real not-found page, or delete the branches (stage 6).

screen: /run/<id>, full: module list; control matrix CT-040, CT-038
title: The connected Run activity has no 'Not assessable' state for a blocked module, and offers 'Start from this run' beside a capped or interrupted run where the matrix records no resume control.

For failed, capped, rejected and interrupted runs the page offers 'Start from this run' (RunProgress.tsx:35,114-119), which opens a new run with the earlier inputs (a new folder, a new cap and new spend), not a resume. Neither could be exercised: the synthetic proof has no blocked module or capped run.
suggested_change: none
ruling_note: OQ-06 decided (R10): add the Not assessable state; keep Start from this run

title: The stage 0 inventory attributes the report frame's controls to C3, C4 and C5, and omits the boundary's Reload page button and the list-layout links by name.
